solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Case for weapon in small taxi seen by poet

indicators.note: seen by places the poet right next to the taxi in the answer

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a cab is a taxi
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A sword's sheath travels in a little cab alongside a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the sheath that holds a sword or dagger.

clue.text: Singers, choosy (not half!) I recognise at first

indicators.note: not half says only half of the word choosy is used, here its first half

parts.note: the first half of the six-letter word choosy

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of I and recognise

parts.note: first letter of I, the word itself
first letter of recognise

explanation.surface: Someone fussy about singers declares they certainly do recognise talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it means take half of choosy: CHO.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is a group of people who sing together.

clue.text: Bird nibbled beside another one

indicators.note: beside puts the second piece right next to the first in the answer

parts.note: bit is the past tense of bite, so nibbled
another bird: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A bird gets pecked at while standing next to a second bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another one' refers back to the definition: another bird, the TERN.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a heron-like wading bird of reedbeds.

clue.text: First-rate catcher? Nothing odd in that

indicators.note: keeping nothing odd means dropping the odd-placed letters of catcher and keeping the even ones

parts.note: the even letters of catcher

explanation.surface: A wicketkeeper or baseball catcher praised as excellent, with nothing strange about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ace as an adjective is informal for excellent or top-class.

clue.text: New version of Art Deco — to a degree

indicators.note: a new version reworks the letters of Art Deco and to into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A revival of Art Deco style is pleasing to some extent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To a degree' reads as 'somewhat'; really 'to' is fodder and 'a degree' points to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctorate is the highest academic qualification a university awards.

clue.text: Mother's meeting son's crowd

indicators.note: meeting joins the son's letter on to the mother's in the answer

parts.note: ma is mother, so mother's gives ma's
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A mother attends a gathering of her son's crowd of friends.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass is a large body of people, a throng.

clue.text: Dormer I think displays good qualities

indicators.note: displays says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dormer window, someone suggests, has architectural virtues.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit means worth or excellence, the good points of something.

clue.text: All set for reform at end of December? Outstanding!

indicators.note: set for reform means the letters of all set are to be reshaped into a new order
end of says take the last letter of December

parts.note: last letter of December

explanation.surface: Everything is ready for reforms at year's end, which is excellent news.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellar, literally of the stars, is used to mean exceptionally good.

clue.text: Nasty riot in southeast leading to soldiers' sudden sally

indicators.note: in places the jumbled riot inside the southeast letters

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for southeast

indicators.note: a nasty riot is a messy one, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A violent disturbance in the southeast leads troops to make a sudden attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A sortie is an attack by troops breaking out from a defended position.

clue.text: Floor covering in vehicle — a favourite

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A rug lies in a car, and it's the household favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpet is a thick textile laid over a floor.

clue.text: Release without charge

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to set loose, a verb

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests letting a prisoner go uncharged; the two halves are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for liberating and an adjective for something given at no cost.

clue.text: Business discussed after hours as spa loth to change tack ultimately

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of spa loth are reordered
ultimately means take the last letter of tack

parts.note: last letter of tack

explanation.surface: Talking work after hours at a spa, someone reluctant to change approach.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop talk is conversation about one's job, especially out of working time.

clue.text: Shop for writers where trains are — supported by Queen

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by puts the queen's letters underneath the station

parts.note: trains stand at a station
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A paper shop at the railway station enjoys royal backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer sells pens, paper and other writing materials; the word names the shop as well as the trader.

clue.text: Dance company not getting approval initially

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: first letter of not
first letter of getting
first letter of approval

explanation.surface: A dance troupe fails to win approval at first.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin American line dance performed in single file.

clue.text: Agree with artist it's unrealistic idea

parts.note: to chime, as in chime with, is to agree
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: Concurring with a painter that a notion is fanciful.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a fanciful, impossible hope or fantasy, named after the mythical monster.

clue.text: Behind in time — some daft error

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Being late is presented as a silly mistake of some kind.
explanation.definitionFit: After means later than, following on in sequence.

clue.text: Typo containing H — cricket side storm

indicators.note: containing means the misprint holds the letter H inside it

parts.note: taken as written
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A misprint with an H and a cricket term combine into a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: A typhoon is a tropical cyclone of the western Pacific.

clue.text: Angry words as aid returned by large family?

indicators.note: by places the family right next to the turned-round aid
returned means the word aid is read backwards

parts.note: a tribe is a large family group

explanation.surface: Help sent back by a big family provokes a furious outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack or rant.

clue.text: Indication of approval to include King in batch of playing cards

indicators.note: to include means the approval mark takes the king's letter inside it

parts.note: a tick marks something as correct or approved
R, Rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A nod of approval for slipping a king into a hand of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games a trick is the set of cards played in one round and won together.

clue.text: Conspiracy cutting India out of experimental programme

indicators.note: cutting says a letter is removed from the programme
out of says where the removed letter comes from: the programme

parts.note: a pilot is a trial episode or test scheme
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A plot to axe India from an experimental scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a secret plan by a group, a scheme.

clue.text: Nothing good kept in reserve

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing
nice means good or pleasant

explanation.surface: Nothing good is being saved for later.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically, something on ice is put aside or postponed for future use.

clue.text: Good to visit West African country, harmless

indicators.note: to visit means the letter goes into the country

parts.note: Benin is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: It's good to visit a West African nation, which is safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Benign means gentle and not harmful, as a benign tumour.

clue.text: Chesspiece that is needed for new recruit

parts.note: the rook, or castle, is a chess piece
IE, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A chess piece is just what a beginner needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a novice or newcomer, originally an army recruit.

clue.text: Farm animal's damage on way up

indicators.note: in a down clue on the way up means the word damage's synonym is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil

explanation.surface: A farm animal causes damage on the uphill track.
explanation.definitionFit: A ram is a male sheep, a typical farmyard animal.

clue.text: Flier's harmless mischief

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a prank or bit of fun

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link: the bird's sense and the prank sense are two meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a singing bird and a playful escapade.

clue.text: Nudge perhaps about person caring for children

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a childminder, or minder, looks after children

explanation.surface: A gentle prod about the babysitter.
explanation.walkthrough: A childminder is a British term for someone paid to look after children in their home.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is one example of a prompt that jogs the memory.
